questions.stem: « Je me lève à six heures et demie. » What does it mean?
options: I go to bed at 6.30
I wake up at 7.30
I wash at half past six
I get up at 6.30
questions.explanation: « Se lever » is to get up and « six heures et demie » is half past six. Going to bed is « se coucher ».

questions.stem: Which word completes « Le matin, nous ___ brossons les dents. »?
options: se
vous
nos
nous
questions.explanation: Reflexive verbs use a pronoun matching the subject: « nous nous brossons ». With parts of the body, French uses « les dents », not « nos dents ».

questions.stem: « D'habitude, je prends le bus, mais aujourd'hui j'y suis allée à pied. » What does the speaker say?
options: She never takes the bus to school
She usually takes the bus but walked today
She usually walks but took the bus today
She always takes the bus to school, even today
questions.explanation: « D'habitude » marks the usual habit and « aujourd'hui » the exception. « Y » stands for the place she went.

questions.stem: « En semaine, on dîne vers vingt heures. » When does the family eat dinner?
options: around 8 pm on weekdays
around 8 pm at weekends
at 10 pm on weekdays
around 6 pm every day
questions.explanation: « En semaine » means on weekdays, and « vers vingt heures » is around 8 pm in the 24-hour clock used in France.

questions.stem: What does « faire la grasse matinée » mean?
options: to get up very early
to have a lazy afternoon
to sleep in late
to eat a big breakfast
questions.explanation: « Faire la grasse matinée » is an idiom for having a sleep-in, usually at the weekend.

questions.stem: « Je fais la vaisselle et mon frère met la table. » Who does what?
options: She cooks dinner and her brother clears the table
She does the washing and her brother does the dishes
She washes the dishes and her brother sets the table
She sets the table and her brother washes the dishes
questions.explanation: « Faire la vaisselle » is to wash the dishes and « mettre la table » to set the table. Doing the laundry is « faire la lessive ».

questions.stem: « Je me couche rarement avant minuit. » What does it mean?
options: I often go to bed before midnight
I never get up before midnight
I always go to bed at midnight
I seldom go to bed before midnight
questions.explanation: « Rarement » means seldom. « Se coucher » is to go to bed, and « avant minuit » is before midnight.

questions.stem: « Pendant la semaine, c'est toujours la course : école, devoirs, entraînement… Heureusement, le week-end, je souffle un peu. » What does the writer say?
options: She runs in races every week and rests at weekends
Weekends are even busier than her weekdays
She has no time to rest during the weekend
Weekdays are a rush, but weekends give her a breather
questions.explanation: « C'est la course » is a figurative rush, not a race, and « souffler » here means to catch your breath. « Heureusement » marks the welcome contrast.

questions.stem: What is « un embouteillage »?
options: a bottle shop
a car park
a road sign
a traffic jam
questions.explanation: « Un embouteillage » (also « un bouchon ») is a traffic jam, typical of city life at rush hour.

questions.stem: « En ville, tout est à portée de main : cinémas, magasins, transports. » What does the writer say about city life?
options: Everything is close at hand
Everything is too expensive
Everything closes too early
Everything is hard to reach
questions.explanation: « À portée de main » means within reach. The list shows the convenience of living in a city.

questions.stem: « À la campagne, on respire mieux, mais on dépend de la voiture pour tout. » What does the speaker say?
options: The country is noisy because of all the cars
The air is better, but you need a car for everything
The air is worse, but public transport is good
Country people walk everywhere and almost never drive
questions.explanation: « On respire mieux » points to cleaner air, and « mais » introduces the drawback: dependence on the car.

questions.stem: What is « un HLM » in France?
options: a flat in public housing at a moderate rent
a luxury apartment in the city centre
a holiday home rented out by the week in summer
a student room in a university hall
questions.explanation: HLM stands for « habitation à loyer modéré », housing at a moderate rent, often in large estates on the edge of cities.

questions.stem: « Mon quartier est très animé le soir. » What does the speaker say?
options: My neighbourhood is quiet in the evening
My neighbourhood is dangerous at night
My neighbourhood is full of animals
My neighbourhood is lively in the evening
questions.explanation: « Le quartier » is the neighbourhood and « animé » means lively, not 'animated' as in cartoons or 'full of animals'.

questions.stem: « Mes grands-parents sont agriculteurs. » What do they do?
options: They are retired teachers
They are shopkeepers
They are farmers
They are gardeners
questions.explanation: « Un agriculteur » works on a farm, « une ferme ». A gardener is « un jardinier ».

questions.stem: « J'habite dans un petit village où il n'y a plus d'école : les enfants vont au collège à vingt kilomètres. » What problem is described?
options: The village has never had a school of its own
The children walk 20 km to school each morning
The village school is too small for 20 children
The village school has closed, so children travel 20 km
questions.explanation: « Il n'y a plus d'école » means there is no longer a school, so it has closed. The text gives the distance but not how the children get there.

questions.stem: What kind of film is « un dessin animé »?
options: a musical
an animated film
a horror film
a nature documentary
questions.explanation: « Un dessin animé » is a cartoon or animated film. A horror film is « un film d'horreur ».

questions.stem: What is « un polar »?
options: a film set in the Arctic
a romantic comedy
a science fiction film
a crime film or novel
questions.explanation: « Un polar » is informal for « un film policier » or a crime novel. It has nothing to do with the poles.

questions.stem: « Le film est sorti en salle mercredi. » What does it mean?
options: The film was released in cinemas on Wednesday
The audience left the cinema on Wednesday
The film was filmed in a hall on Wednesday
The film will be shown on national TV on Wednesday
questions.explanation: « Sortir en salle » means to be released in cinemas. In France, new films usually come out on Wednesdays.

questions.stem: « La séance de 20 h est complète. » What does it mean?
options: The 8 pm screening is sold out
The 8 pm screening has finished
The 8 pm screening is cancelled
The 8 pm screening is half empty
questions.explanation: « Une séance » is a screening or session, and « complète » means full. Choose another session or book ahead.

questions.stem: In cinema, who is « le réalisateur »?
options: the lead actor
the director
the producer
the scriptwriter
questions.explanation: « Réaliser un film » means to direct it. The scriptwriter is « le scénariste » and the producer « le producteur ».

questions.stem: « Les effets spéciaux sont bluffants. » What is the reviewer's opinion?
options: The special effects are fake
The special effects are dated
The special effects are missing
The special effects are amazing
questions.explanation: « Bluffant » is informal for stunning or impressive. The reviewer is amazed by the effects, not saying they look fake.

questions.stem: « J'ai trouvé l'histoire un peu tirée par les cheveux, mais les acteurs sont géniaux. » What is the reviewer's view?
options: The actors are poor, but the plot is clever
The plot and the actors are both excellent
The actors' hairstyles spoil the story
The plot is far-fetched, but the actors are great
questions.explanation: « Tiré par les cheveux » (literally pulled by the hair) means far-fetched. « Mais » sets the weak plot against the « géniaux » actors.

questions.stem: « Les Français vont encore beaucoup au cinéma : c'est une sortie en famille ou entre amis. » What does this say about French lifestyles?
options: Cinemas in France are only for families with children
Going to the cinema is too expensive for most people
Going to the cinema remains a popular social outing
The French now watch films mostly alone at home
questions.explanation: « Encore beaucoup » means still a lot, and « une sortie » is an outing, shared with family or friends.

questions.stem: « Mon chanteur préféré sort un nouvel album. » What is happening?
options: My favourite singer is going on a new tour
My favourite singer is buying a new album
My favourite singer is releasing a new album
My favourite singer is leaving his band
questions.explanation: « Sortir un album » means to release it. « Nouvel » is the form of « nouveau » used before a vowel.

questions.stem: In a song, what is « le refrain »?
options: the verse
the melody
the title
the chorus
questions.explanation: « Le refrain » is the chorus, repeated between « les couplets », the verses.

questions.stem: « Les billets pour le concert se sont vendus en dix minutes. » What happened?
options: The concert started ten minutes late
The concert lasted only ten minutes
Tickets go on sale in ten minutes
The concert sold out in ten minutes
questions.explanation: « Se vendre » here has a passive meaning, 'to be sold', and the passé composé shows the sale is over.

questions.stem: « Mon frère adore chanter, mais il chante faux. » What does the speaker say?
options: Her brother sings out of tune
Her brother sings in secret
Her brother sings very loudly
Her brother sings fake songs
questions.explanation: « Chanter faux » means to sing out of tune; singing in tune is « chanter juste ».

questions.stem: « Cette chanson me rappelle mes vacances au Québec : dès que je l'entends, j'ai envie de danser. » What effect does the song have?
options: It brings back holiday memories and makes her want to dance
It reminds her to book her next summer holiday in Québec
It was written in Québec during her last holiday
It makes her sad because the holiday is over
questions.explanation: « Rappeler » means to remind of, and « dès que » plus the present gives an automatic reaction: every time she hears it, she wants to dance.
